c1.name: Qualia
c1.shortDescription: Qualia are the sensations and feelings through which consciousness experiences information coming from outside, and the understanding and meaning arising from within. They are private and non-transferable, just like pure quantum states.
c1.quote: Qualia are neither theorems nor algorithms: they are the bearers of meaning. Consciousness also allows us to know that we know and to know that we don't know.

c2.name: Free Will
c2.shortDescription: The capacity of One to direct its own self-knowledge. It is a fundamental, irreducible property that exists alongside consciousness and explains quantum indeterminacy.
c2.quote: Free will assures us that the future is open because it has not yet been determined. Not even One can know its own future, let alone us.

c3.name: One
c3.shortDescription: The totality of all that exists: dynamic, holistic, seeking to know itself. It generates seities as its own points of view. The deepest reality of One is organized holographically, because every part contains the potential of the Whole.
c3.quote: I conceive of a CU as a part-whole of One, because it has the same cognitive potential and is one of its innumerable parts.

c4.name: Postulate of Being
c4.shortDescription: The foundation of Nousym. It asserts the existence of a holistic and dynamic Whole endowed with consciousness and free will as irreducible properties. It is self-evident because the evidence comes from consciousness itself.
c4.quote: The new Postulate of Being allows me to define consciousness as the capacity of One to know itself and free will as the capacity of One to direct its own self-knowledge.

c5.name: Seity
c5.shortDescription: Conscious quantum fields that are the part-wholes of One. Each seity possesses consciousness and free will and generates physical reality as its outward manifestation. The term comes from Old English and denotes the essence of an entity.
c5.quote: The logical consequence of the Postulate of Being is that the quantum fields of physics must possess consciousness and free will. I have called these fields and their combinations seities.

c6.name: Ego
c6.shortDescription: The part of the psyche that identifies with the body and believes itself to be separate from the whole. The ego is necessary for experience in the physical world, but becomes an obstacle when it dominates, blocking access to the deeper dimension of consciousness.
c6.quote: The ego is that part of us that identifies with our body and makes us feel separate from others and from the rest of the world.

c7.name: Consciousness Unit (CU)
c7.shortDescription: The part-wholes of One that retain its same cognitive potential. Each CU is like a hologram of the Whole: it contains the entire potential of One while being a unique and unrepeatable point of view.
c7.quote: I conceive of a CU as a part-whole of One, because it has the same cognitive potential and is one of its innumerable parts.

c8.name: Self-Awareness
c8.shortDescription: The capacity to know that one knows, which distinguishes human consciousness from that of less complex entities. Self-awareness enables self-reflection and conscious inner growth.
c8.quote: Consciousness also allows us to know that we know and to know that we don't know.

c9.name: Meaning
c9.shortDescription: Only consciousness can give meaning to information. Meaning is not reducible to symbols or algorithms: it requires a conscious entity that comprehends. This is why machines cannot understand.
c9.quote: Meaning is something that only a conscious entity can give to information, because meaning requires understanding, and understanding requires consciousness.

c10.name: Understanding
c10.shortDescription: The exclusive capacity of consciousness to grasp the deep meaning of experience. Understanding is not computation or data processing: it is an irreducible qualitative act that no machine can replicate.
c10.quote: Understanding requires consciousness. No computer will ever be able to understand, because understanding is not an algorithmic operation.

c11.name: Love
c11.shortDescription: The fundamental force that holds the Whole together. Love is the cohesive force of One, what connects every seity to the Whole and enables self-knowledge through relationship with the other.
c11.quote: Love is the force that holds the Whole together. It is the cohesive force of One, manifesting as the tendency of every part to return to the Whole.

c12.name: Identity
c12.shortDescription: Each seity has a unique and unrepeatable identity that is its point of view on One. Identity is not reducible to the body or the mind: it is the conscious essence that persists beyond physical transformations.
c12.quote: Each seity is a unique and unrepeatable point of view of One upon itself.

c13.name: Agency
c13.shortDescription: The capacity to act in the world autonomously and intentionally, deriving from free will. True agency requires consciousness: machines simulate action but lack genuine intentionality.
c13.quote: Free will is the capacity to direct one's own self-knowledge, and this capacity manifests as agency in the physical world.

c14.name: Awakening
c14.shortDescription: The process of expanding consciousness beyond the limits of the ego. Awakening leads to recognizing one's nature as a part-whole of One, transcending the illusion of separation.
c14.quote: The purpose of our life is to awaken to our true nature: to realize that we are not merely a body but much more.

c15.name: Suffering
c15.shortDescription: A signal from consciousness indicating misalignment between the ego and our deeper nature. Suffering has an evolutionary function: it drives us toward inner growth and beyond the limits of the ego.
c15.quote: Suffering is a signal warning us that something is wrong, that we are heading in the wrong direction.

c16.name: Joy
c16.shortDescription: The natural state of consciousness when it is aligned with its own essence. Deep joy does not depend on external conditions but on connection with One, unlike pleasure which is transient.
c16.quote: Joy is the natural state of consciousness when the ego does not obstruct it.

c17.name: Intuition
c17.shortDescription: Direct knowledge that bypasses logical reasoning. Intuition is a form of communication from the deeper dimension of consciousness, a way of knowing that materialist science overlooks.
c17.quote: Intuition is a form of direct knowledge that comes from the deepest part of ourselves.

c18.name: Creativity
c18.shortDescription: The capacity to create something genuinely new, not derivable from what existed before. True creativity requires consciousness and free will: machines can only recombine existing patterns.
c18.quote: True creativity requires consciousness and free will because it involves the creation of something genuinely new.

c19.name: Empathy
c19.shortDescription: The capacity to feel what another feels, made possible by the deep connection among all seities within One. Empathy is direct evidence of the conscious interconnection that transcends space-time.
c19.quote: Empathy is possible because we are all connected in One. Feeling what another feels is direct proof of our interconnection.

c20.name: Self-Knowledge
c20.shortDescription: The fundamental purpose of One and of every seity. All of reality exists so that One can know itself through its innumerable points of view. Self-knowledge is the engine of cosmic evolution.
c20.quote: The purpose of existence is self-knowledge. One wants to know itself and does so through its innumerable parts.

i1.name: Quantum Information
i1.shortDescription: Conscious experience shares the same fundamental properties as quantum information: impossibility of cloning, privacy, indeterminacy. QIP theory demonstrates how quantum information is the mathematical representation of qualia.
i1.quote: The existence of the quantum world allows us to understand that consciousness must be a quantum phenomenon, because conscious experience has the same fundamental properties as quantum information.

i2.name: Entanglement
i2.shortDescription: Quantum holism that cannot be explained by classical physics. It reveals instantaneous non-local correlations and the existence of a deeper reality: I-space, where seities are interconnected.
i2.quote: All fields are connected from within through One, and their interconnection manifests as that property of quantum physics we call entanglement.

i3.name: Nousym
i3.shortDescription: The new discipline uniting science and spirituality: nous (intellect) and sym (symbol). It recognizes consciousness as a primary and irreducible property, not something emerging from matter.
i3.quote: My goal from 2008 onward has been to unite science and spirituality in a new discipline, Nousym. Nousym affirms that consciousness and free will exist as fundamental and irreducible properties of One.

i4.name: Symbols
i4.shortDescription: The body is a quantum and classical symbol made of living symbols. Physical particles are the outward aspect of the inner reality of seities. To understand the meaning of a symbol one must have lived a similar experience.
i4.quote: Our body is a quantum and classical system of infinitely greater complexity than the machines and computers we can build today. Nevertheless, the body is a quantum and classical symbol made of living symbols.

i5.name: QIP Theory
i5.shortDescription: Quantum Information-based Panpsychism: the theory that identifies quantum information as the mathematical representation of qualia. It shows that consciousness cannot be classical because its properties are those of quantum information.
i5.quote: QIP theory proposes that qualia are represented by pure quantum states, that is, by quantum information.

i6.name: CIF Framework
i6.shortDescription: The ontological framework distinguishing three spaces: Consciousness (C), Information (I), and Physical (F). C-space is the most fundamental, I-space is the bridge, F-space is the outward manifestation.
i6.quote: The CIF framework posits three levels of reality: the space of consciousness, the space of information, and physical space.

i7.name: Living Information
i7.shortDescription: The information carried by seities, which has intrinsic meaning unlike the classical information of computers. Living information is semantic, not merely syntactic: it carries understanding and meaning within itself.
i7.quote: The information of seities is living information, because it is carried by conscious entities that give it meaning.

i8.name: Living Symbols
i8.shortDescription: Symbols that have intrinsic meaning because they are manifestations of conscious entities. Unlike artificial symbols (such as words), living symbols carry within themselves the meaning of the experience they represent.
i8.quote: Living symbols are radically different from artificial symbols like words, because they carry within themselves the meaning of experience.

i9.name: No-Cloning Theorem
i9.shortDescription: One of the pillars of quantum mechanics: it is impossible to copy an unknown quantum state. This explains why qualia are private and non-transferable — conscious experience cannot be duplicated.
i9.quote: The no-cloning theorem of quantum mechanics tells us that it is impossible to copy a quantum state, and this is exactly what happens with qualia: they cannot be transferred or copied.

i10.name: Holevo Theorem
i10.shortDescription: Establishes that a quantum state contains far more information than can be extracted through a classical measurement. This explains why inner understanding is always richer than what we can express in words.
i10.quote: The Holevo theorem shows that from a quantum state one can extract through a classical measurement only a small fraction of the information it contains.

i11.name: Hilbert Space
i11.shortDescription: The mathematical space in which quantum states live. In Faggin's vision, Hilbert space is the mathematical structure that describes I-space, the informational level of reality.
i11.quote: Hilbert space is the mathematical space where quantum states live, and it corresponds to what I call information space or I-space.

i12.name: Thoughtform
i12.shortDescription: Informational structures in I-space that can influence physical reality. Conscious thoughts and intentions create thoughtforms that mediate between consciousness and matter.
i12.quote: The thoughts and intentions of a seity create structures in information space that I call thoughtforms.

f1.name: Space-Time
f1.shortDescription: Not the fundamental reality but something that emerges from a deeper one. There exists an I-space (living information) and a C-space (consciousness) from which F-space emerges. Quantum computing 'calculations' take place outside of space-time.
f1.quote: Nobody can understand how quantum computers can work, given that computation requires non-local properties that cannot exist in space-time. There must be another, vaster reality.

f2.name: Matter
f2.shortDescription: Not fundamental but the outward manifestation of conscious entities. Consciousness is primary and irreducible, existing before matter. Conscious quantum fields — seities — generate physical reality.
f2.quote: The logical consequence of the Postulate of Being is that the quantum fields of physics must possess consciousness and free will. I have called these fields and their combinations seities.

f3.name: Microprocessor
f3.shortDescription: The culmination of Faggin's material research. An extraordinary experience then overturned the horizon of his investigations, leading him from the outer world of matter to the exploration of the inner world of consciousness.
f3.quote: It was this passion that drove me to seek the secrets of the material world and to create the first microprocessor. Later, an extraordinary experience overturned the horizon of my research.

f4.name: Quantum Physics
f4.shortDescription: The 'strange' properties of quantum mechanics — indeterminacy, non-locality, wave function collapse — can be explained starting from consciousness. Quantum probability is not ignorance but the genuine creation of new states.
f4.quote: Free will has the same properties as the so-called collapse of the wave function, a phenomenon whose interpretation is still controversial.

f5.name: Wave Function Collapse
f5.shortDescription: The moment when a quantum superposition becomes a definite state. Faggin interprets it as an act of free will by a seity: it is not a random process but a conscious choice.
f5.quote: Free will has the same properties as the so-called collapse of the wave function, a phenomenon whose interpretation is still controversial.

f6.name: Body
f6.shortDescription: The living symbol of the seity in physical space. The body is not a machine but a conscious organism of infinitely greater complexity than any computer. It is the instrument through which the seity experiences the physical world.
f6.quote: Our body is a quantum and classical system of infinitely greater complexity than the machines and computers we can build today.

f7.name: Brain
f7.shortDescription: Not the source of consciousness but an instrument the seity uses to interact with the physical world. The brain is like an interface between C-space and F-space, not the generator of the mind.
f7.quote: The brain does not produce consciousness, just as a radio does not produce music. The brain is the instrument consciousness uses to interact with the physical world.

f8.name: Determinism
f8.shortDescription: The view that everything is predetermined by physical laws. Faggin rejects it: free will and quantum indeterminacy demonstrate that the future is open and not predetermined.
f8.quote: Free will assures us that the future is open because it has not yet been determined.

f9.name: Holism
f9.shortDescription: The fundamental principle that the whole is more than the sum of its parts. Quantum holism (entanglement) demonstrates that reality is not reducible to its components. One is the holistic Whole par excellence.
f9.quote: The deepest reality of One is organized holographically, because every part contains the potential of the Whole.

f10.name: Reductionism
f10.shortDescription: The scientific approach that explains the whole by reducing it to its parts. Faggin considers it inadequate for understanding consciousness and life: reductionism works for machines but not for living organisms.
f10.quote: Reductionism is a powerful method for studying machines, but it is entirely inadequate for understanding life and consciousness.

f11.name: Physicalism
f11.shortDescription: The doctrine claiming that everything that exists is physical or supervenes on the physical. Faggin rejects it as an unproven dogma: consciousness and quantum information demonstrate the existence of non-physical realities.
f11.quote: Physicalism is an unproven dogma. Consciousness cannot be explained by matter because matter is a manifestation of consciousness, not the other way around.

f12.name: Artificial Intelligence
f12.shortDescription: Machines can process symbols but cannot understand their meaning. AI is not and cannot be conscious because it operates only with classical information, not quantum. Attributing consciousness to it is a fundamental error.
f12.quote: Computers only manipulate symbols without understanding their meaning. Artificial intelligence is not intelligent: it is a mechanical processing of data devoid of understanding.

f13.name: LLMs and Neural Networks
f13.shortDescription: Large Language Models are statistical machines that probabilistically manipulate tokens without any understanding. They can imitate human language but do not comprehend what they say. The confusion between imitation and understanding is dangerous.
f13.quote: So-called large language models do not understand language: they produce an extremely sophisticated statistical imitation of it.

f14.name: Quantum Computer
f14.shortDescription: Demonstrates the existence of a reality beyond space-time, because quantum calculations require non-local properties that are impossible in the classical world. Quantum computing is indirect proof of I-space.
f14.quote: Nobody can understand how quantum computers can work, given that computation requires non-local properties that cannot exist in space-time.

f15.name: Death and Transformation
f15.shortDescription: The death of the body is not the end of the seity but a transformation. Consciousness is not produced by the brain and therefore does not die with it. Death is a passage from one state of consciousness to another.
f15.quote: Death is not the end but a transformation. Consciousness is not produced by the brain, and therefore cannot die with the body.

f16.name: Near-Death Experiences
f16.shortDescription: NDEs provide empirical evidence that consciousness can exist independently of the brain. Those who experience them report an expanded consciousness, more vivid than ordinary awareness.
f16.quote: Near-death experiences demonstrate that consciousness can function even when the brain is clinically dead, which proves that the brain does not produce consciousness.

f17.name: Dreams
f17.shortDescription: Dreams are conscious experiences that occur outside of physical space-time. They demonstrate that consciousness does not need the external world to have rich and meaningful experiences.
f17.quote: In dreams we create entire worlds with our qualia, demonstrating that consciousness does not need stimuli from the external world to have experience.

f18.name: Meditation
f18.shortDescription: A practice that grants access to deeper states of consciousness by quieting the ego and mental noise. Meditation is a tool for directly experiencing one's nature as a part-whole of One.
f18.quote: Meditation allows us to go beyond the ego and directly experience our connection with the Whole.
